pr.title: Anonymous: Add configurable device limit

raw_findings.body: TypeScript infers this class field's type as the literal `undefined` instead of `number | undefined`, so any subsequent assignment of a number to this property fails type-checking, and callers relying on the declared `number | undefined` type get an always-undefined value at the type level, masking real runtime values.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Type-checking allows an always-undefined-typed property to silently diverge from the actual runtime numeric value, hiding compile-time errors elsewhere in the codebase.
raw_findings.impact: TypeScript infers this class field's type as the literal `undefined` instead of `number | undefined`, so any subsequent assignment of a number to this property fails type-checking, and callers relying on the declared `number | undefined` type get an always-undefined value at the type level, masking real runtime values.
raw_findings.root_cause: Missing explicit type annotation on a class field initialized with `undefined`, causing TypeScript to narrow-infer the type instead of matching the interface's `number | undefined`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly annotate the field as other optional fields in this class do, e.g. `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.
raw_findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit field typed too narrowly, breaking GrafanaConfig contract
raw_findings.trigger: Any code path that later assigns a numeric value to config.anonymousDeviceLimit (e.g. bootstrap merge of server settings) or reads it expecting `number | undefined` per the GrafanaConfig interface.

raw_findings.body: Several new devices can be inserted concurrently despite the configured device limit, causing the enforced anonymousDeviceLimit to be exceeded, defeating the feature's purpose.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent execution paths both observe stale state and both proceed to write, violating the invariant the check was meant to enforce.
raw_findings.impact: Several new devices can be inserted concurrently despite the configured device limit, causing the enforced anonymousDeviceLimit to be exceeded, defeating the feature's purpose.
raw_findings.root_cause: Device-limit enforcement uses a separate read (CountDevices) followed by a separate write (insert/update) without any locking or transactional guarantee, creating a check-then-act race.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Enforce the limit atomically, e.g. via a unique constraint plus a single INSERT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit inside a transaction, or use a DB-level advisory lock/transaction around the count-then-act sequence.
raw_findings.title: TOCTOU race allows device limit bypass under concurrent requests
raw_findings.trigger: Multiple concurrent anonymous requests with distinct new device IDs arrive while the current device count is exactly at (deviceLimit - 1), so each request's CountDevices check independently observes a count below the limit before any of them commits its insert.

raw_findings.body: Every anonymous request incurs added latency for the DB round-trip on the authentication hot path, and if the client cancels/times out the original request, ctx cancellation can abort the DB write mid-flight, whereas previously the write ran fire-and-forget with an independent timeout and was resilient to request cancellation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authentication requests are now coupled to database write latency and cancellation, degrading responsiveness under load or when device DB writes are slow.
raw_findings.impact: Every anonymous request incurs added latency for the DB round-trip on the authentication hot path, and if the client cancels/times out the original request, ctx cancellation can abort the DB write mid-flight, whereas previously the write ran fire-and-forget with an independent timeout and was resilient to request cancellation.
raw_findings.root_cause: The previous goroutine-based asynchronous device tagging with an independent timeout context was removed and replaced with a direct synchronous call using the request's own context.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep device tagging asynchronous (or use a bounded background context) so authentication latency is not coupled to the device-tagging DB write, while still allowing propagation of ErrDeviceLimitReached through the synchronous path when limit is enforced.
raw_findings.title: Anonymous authentication now blocks synchronously on device-tagging DB write
raw_findings.trigger: Every anonymous authentication request now executes TagDevice (a synchronous DB insert/update/count) inline before Authenticate returns, using the caller's own request context instead of the previously used detached background context.

raw_findings.body: There is no test asserting that Authenticate returns a non-nil error (and denies the identity) when the device limit is reached, so a future regression in this new error-propagation path would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent regression risk: incorrect handling of ErrDeviceLimitReached (e.g. accidentally swallowing it) would go undetected by existing tests.
raw_findings.impact: There is no test asserting that Authenticate returns a non-nil error (and denies the identity) when the device limit is reached, so a future regression in this new error-propagation path would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: New conditional error-propagation branch was added to Authenticate without accompanying unit test coverage.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test for Anonymous.Authenticate using a fake anonDeviceService.TagDevice returning anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached and assert Authenticate returns a nil identity and the wrapped error.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage for Authenticate's new device-limit error propagation
raw_findings.trigger: An anonymous authentication attempt occurs when the configured device limit has been reached, so TagDevice returns anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached.

raw_findings.body: The new `device_limit` ini key is functional but absent from conf/defaults.ini, so operators/documentation consumers have no discoverable reference for this new configuration option or its default value.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reference documentation for configuration settings becomes stale/incomplete relative to actual parsed settings.
raw_findings.impact: The new `device_limit` ini key is functional but absent from conf/defaults.ini, so operators/documentation consumers have no discoverable reference for this new configuration option or its default value.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new configuration key was wired into Cfg parsing without updating the corresponding entry in conf/defaults.ini.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a `device_limit = 0` entry with an explanatory comment to the [auth.anonymous] section of conf/defaults.ini.
raw_findings.title: New device_limit ini setting undocumented in conf/defaults.ini
raw_findings.trigger: An operator inspects conf/defaults.ini (the canonical reference for all configurable settings under [auth.anonymous]) to discover or document the new device_limit option.

raw_findings.body: The device-limit window used for CountDevices/updateDevice can silently diverge from the window used for listing devices in the API and the usage-stats window in impl.go, producing inconsistent behavior across the feature.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Configuration drift between duplicated constants leads to inconsistent time windows used for related functionality without any compiler warning.
raw_findings.impact: The device-limit window used for CountDevices/updateDevice can silently diverge from the window used for listing devices in the API and the usage-stats window in impl.go, producing inconsistent behavior across the feature.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces a second, independently-declared `anonymousDeviceExpiration` constant with the same value already used elsewhere (thirtyDays in impl.go, and the renamed constant in api.go), instead of sharing a single source of truth.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Define the 30-day expiration constant once (e.g. exported from anonstore) and reuse it from api.go and impl.go instead of redeclaring the same literal duration in multiple packages.
raw_findings.title: Duplicated 30-day expiration constant introduced across packages
raw_findings.trigger: A future change to the anonymous-device retention/expiration window (e.g. changing it from 30 to 45 days) is made in one of the now three independent definitions (anonimpl.thirtyDays, api.anonymousDeviceExpiration, anonstore.anonymousDeviceExpiration) but not the others.
